claims.detail: Every one of 3 registered UCP panel scenarios has a held-out interval favoring adaptive stopping over costed search-all.
limitations: Merchant domains are replay cards, not verified independent sellers or checkout offers.
Inspection costs are declared rate-card scenarios, not observed UCP billing.
Same-SKU decks establish catalog identity but not shipping, tax, or availability at checkout.
claims.scope: Same-SKU, USD seller decks with at least three observed UCP merchant domains from ten registered quality-included daily panel dates. All dates for a SKU stay together in either calibration or held-out evaluation. Search-all opens every card and pays every declared inspection cost; the result is not pooled with Shopify decks.
claims.statement: Across every registered inspection-cost scenario, adaptive recalled search reliably improves held-out total cost over costed search-all on the frozen September 2026 direct-merchant UCP panel series.

claims.detail: At zero cost search-all is favorable; at 0.01x and 0.1x the interval crosses zero; at 1x and 10x adaptive stopping is favorable.
limitations: The multipliers are counterfactual cost sensitivity values, not observed billing.
Merchant domains are replay cards, not verified independent sellers or checkout offers.
The result is clustered by SKU and does not make dates independent evidence.
claims.scope: Same SKU-clustered UCP daily-panel replay as UCP-PANDORA-REPLAY-001. The five registered multipliers scale the complete catalog-expansion per-inspection cost while holding its dated September 2026 provider rates and workload composition fixed. It is a sensitivity result, not observed provider billing.
claims.statement: In the frozen September 2026 UCP recall-aware panel replay, adaptive search reliably improves held-out total cost at the current catalog-expansion market rate and at ten times that workload. Search-all reliably improves at zero cost, while one-hundredth and one-tenth of the workload are inconclusive.

claims.detail: Shopify adaptive-versus-search-all intervals favor adaptive stopping only in the registered long-horizon scenario.
limitations: Seller-order permutations are repeated replays, not independent products.
Only the complete 39-query prefix of 48 registered deep queries is analyzed.
Inspection costs use declared provider rate cards and workloads, not observed Shopify billing.
claims.scope: Forty title-normalized product decks from one frozen Shopify collection, 24 used for calibration and 16 held out, evaluated across three registered declared real-dollar inspection-cost scenarios. Search-all opens every card and pays every declared inspection cost. The post-collection identity revision limits external interpretation but does not alter the registered held-out calculation.
claims.statement: In an exploratory frozen Shopify seller-deck replay built with a post-collection title-identity revision, adaptive recalled search reliably improves held-out total cost over costed search-all in the registered long-horizon scenario, but not in the two lower-cost scenarios.
